data: Thor and Delta pad pair: Spirit, Opportunity, Pathfinder, MESSENGER, Dawn; demolished in 2018

Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 17 (later SLC-17) was a pair of pads, 17A and 17B, built in 1956 by the US Air Force for the Thor missile; NASA's Kennedy history page dates the first Thor launches to 25 January 1957 from 17B and 30 August 1957 from 17A. Its first orbital-class attempt was Pioneer 0, a Thor-Able lunar probe lost 73.6 seconds after liftoff from 17A on 17 August 1958. The Air Force handed Pad 17A to NASA in 1965 and took it back in 1988 for Delta II; Wikipedia counts 321 launches from the two pads, the last from 17B being GRAIL on 10 September 2011, and both towers were demolished on 12 July 2018. Sources: NASA KSC 'About Launch Complex 17' (archived), Wikipedia (SLC-17, Pioneer 0, mission articles), Spaceflight Now; coordinates from Wikipedia and Wikidata.

Two Thor-lineage pads, 17A and 17B, near the beach at Cape Canaveral. The Air Force built them in 1956 for the Thor missile, then upgraded them in the early 1960s for Thor-derived rockets, which became the Delta family. Pioneer 0, an attempted lunar orbiter, was lost here on 17 August 1958 when its Thor-Able exploded 73.6 seconds after liftoff. In the Delta II years the pads sent NASA probes to Mars and beyond: NEAR Shoemaker and Mars Pathfinder in 1996, Spirit and Opportunity in 2003, MESSENGER in 2004, Phoenix and Dawn in 2007. The Delta III flew three times from 17B between 1998 and 2000 before the programme was abandoned. The last launch was GRAIL on 10 September 2011, and both towers were demolished on 12 July 2018.
First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid (433 Eros, 2000) and first soft landing on any small body (2001-02-12)
First wheels on Mars; demonstrated airbag landing
First of the Mars Exploration Rover twins; longest-lived rover until passed by Opportunity
Held the Mars driving record (45.16 km) until Perseverance passed it in October 2026; 14-year surface lifetime against a 90-sol design
First spacecraft to orbit Mercury; first complete surface map of the innermost planet
First confirmation of water ice in the Martian arctic regolith; first soft propulsive Mars landing since Viking 2
First mission to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies — Vesta, then Ceres
Twin to Spirit; nearly 15-year Mars operation
First Mercury orbiter — 6 planetary gravity assists over 6.6 years to bleed energy before insertion in 2011
Confirmed water ice in Martian soil
Only spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial worlds — Vesta then Ceres via ion propulsion
Cape Canaveral Mercury-Atlas pad — launched all 4 orbital Mercury flights (Glenn / Carpenter / Schirra / Cooper, 1962-1963)
Cape Canaveral Mercury-Redstone pad — launched Freedom 7 (Shepard, 1961-05-05) and Liberty Bell 7 (Grissom, 1961-07-21)
Sputnik 1 (1957). Vostok 1 — Gagarin (1961). Five hundred and forty Soyuz launches from a single pad.
Active Soyuz crewed pad — every ISS Soyuz crew rotation since 2020 has lifted from Site 31
NASA pad at Cape Canaveral (1961-68) — first Saturn I; Apollo 1 fire site 1967-01-27; Apollo 7 first crewed launch 1968-10-11
Polar / sun-synchronous gateway — Falcon 9 to Starlink + national-security + earth-observation
